spec.name: four_seam_wrap_mixer_v1
spec.limitations: Expected failure mode: the four fixed rotations are hard seams in an otherwise public straight-line program, so a chosen-plaintext structural attack should bisect the buffer seam by seam and recover key bytes incrementally; I expect the bounded oracle to need on the order of a few thousand chosen pairs, more than for my earlier single-rotation designs but still tractable. Differential comparison should work bit-wise across each rotation because rotations are byte-aligned and the only messiness is carry propagation during additions, so flip patterns that avoid carry chains stay traceable. Key-schedule analysis should partially succeed: the 16-byte round-robin key means positions 16 apart share key bytes, and 16-aligned differentials can be walked through the seams to cancel key contributions. I do not expect GF(2) linear algebra to apply directly due to carries, but I make no claim the modular equations are hard on short messages. Degeneracies: for a one-byte message every rotation is trivial, and when the message length divides 211, 89, 131 or 59 the corresponding rotation is the identity, removing that seam; short messages are weakly mixed. Equal plaintexts under the same key give equal ciphertexts.
spec.math: F = P20 o ... o P1, applied in listed order: R211, K (add_key), C (chain_add running sum), rol3, X (xor_key), R89, A128, Z (chain_xor), K, rol5, R131, A46, C, X, rol7, R59, A201, Z, K, rol1. Every component is a bijection on (Z/256)^L: byte additions and XORs invert with the same key byte or constant, rol inverts by (8-n) mod 8, chain_add inverts by differencing y[i]-y[i-1], chain_xor by y[i] xor y[i-1], and buffer rotations invert by L-n, so F is bijective. Nonlinearity over GF(2) is carried by the modular additions and running sums; diffusion comes from the four buffer rotations, which relocate bytes across four distinct cut points so dependencies run both below and above each position through the prefix runs.
spec.assumptions: The key is a uniformly random 16-byte value used round-robin by position and reused across messages with no nonce; the program is public; message length L is arbitrary (at least 1 byte) and known to both parties; per-byte rotations are modulo 8 and whole-buffer rotations modulo L; equal plaintexts under the same key give identical ciphertexts.
